test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He asked me if I had ever been to the Louvre.

options.text: He said, "You have ever been to the Louvre?"
He asked, "Do you ever go to the Louvre?"
He asked me, "Have you been to the Louvre?"
He said to me, "Have you ever been to the Louvre?"

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. "He said to me, 'Have you ever been to the Louvre?'".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **indirect speech**, where a question is being reported.
 
• To convert indirect speech into direct speech for a question, the sentence must:
 
 
• Include quotation marks.
 
• Use the exact question format and wording.
 
• Retain the original tense of the question.
 
 
 
• In direct speech, the question is typically introduced with a reporting verb like "said to" or "asked."

Correct sentence: *He said to me, "Have you ever been to the Louvre?"*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for converting indirect speech to direct speech:**

 
 
• Remove introductory words like "He asked me" or "He said."
 
• Use quotation marks to enclose the exact words spoken.
 
• Ensure proper punctuation, such as a question mark for questions.
 
• Preserve the tense from the original direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Indirect: She asked if I was coming tomorrow. → Direct: She asked, "Are you coming tomorrow?"
 
• Indirect: He wondered whether it was raining. → Direct: He said, "Is it raining?"
